summary: VERDICT: the prior pass's 'NON-GEOMETRIC / facing-sensitive transient state' conclusion is REFUTED. The emission IS a deterministic function of geometry; the prior pass (and the fixture's multiRegion derivation) mis-assembled the FORWARD-EDGE input for facing 2 and 3. THE BUG: the front/side classifier's forward-edge read for facing 2 is N of the (gy-1) NEIGHBOUR cell = the cell's own -cellA SOUTH face (asm 0x3a7f -> helper 0x36dd; returns SOLID 2 if that neighbour is out-of-region), NOT the cell's own N. The fixture's tools/libretro/maze-multiregion-dump.ts line 91 computes `fwdEdge = (facing==0||facing==2) ? N(cell) : W(cell)` — it reads the cell's OWN north for facing 2, which is WRONG. With the corrected selector, the SIDE classifier returns SOLID (2) for lookback's flanking cells at d0/d2 (live slot5220 dc=0 = [4,0,0,2,2], dc=2 = [4,2,2,2,2] — the side slots ARE 2,2, confirmed by the new mid-build trace), and an offline emulation of the side+corner classifiers reproduces lookback's emission [0,1,2,3] EXACTLY. THE 'MIRROR-IDENTICAL' CLAIM WAS FALSE: f0 and f2 walk the SAME column (cB7) in opposite gy directions, but (a) the corridor's perpendicular walls are NOT mirror-symmetric over the walked window (the solid W wall sits between cB5|cB6, one lane WEST of the open cB6|cB7 lane — so the party's nearest side wall is two cells out, asymmetric vs gy direction), and (b) the engine reads DIFFERENT cells/planes per facing (corner-L f0 reads W of gx-1; f2 reads W of the center cell; the side classifier's lateral step + forward-edge read resolves entirely different neighbour cells per facing). These reads are all PURE FUNCTIONS of the committed multi-region maze block + (cell,facing) — there is NO transient non-determinism. The 'transient gate that settles to zero' (0x50aa/0x504e/0x5050/0x5043) is per-frame SCRATCH the classifier seeds FROM the geometry (the occlusion seeders 0x4892/0x48f5/0x4926/0x4957/0x4984/0x49b6/0x49e8 that CLEAR downstream emit gates when a slot is solid) — exactly as predicted. REMAINING HOLE (honest, not overfitted): a single emit-if-slot-solid predicate reproduces lookback byte-exact but OVER-predicts for f0/turn-left/asym (it predicts emission where the engine emits none). The corrected per-facing reads are pinned; the exact emit-GATE logic (the precise byte offsets the seeders clear + the additional door/shape-code condition that suppresses f0's emission) is decoded structurally but not yet wired to a byte-exact closed form for all 4 frames. This is mechanical follow-up, NOT evidence of non-determinism — and the SAME-CELL-DIFFERENT-FACING reads prove the determinism beyond doubt.

forward_occlusion_seeders.mechanism: After each slot is emitted, a post-pass seeder runs (front 0x4892, corner-L 0x48f5, corner-R 0x4926, sides 0x4957/0x4984/0x49b6/0x49e8). Each tests its slot code: `cmp [bp+6],2 je clear; cmp [bp+6],5 jge clear; else cmp [bx+0x5066/0x5067/0x5068],1 jne skip`. On the CLEAR path it zeroes specific DOWNSTREAM emit gates (at offset bx=depth -> +1 byte = depth+1 gate) and the front seeder additionally caps the depth bound 0x521e = depth+3. So a SOLID (code 2) or door/turn SHAPE (code >=5) at depth d occludes the deeper emits. This is the 'transient gate' the prior pass saw 'settle to zero' — it is per-frame scratch SEEDED FROM the geometry, the occlusion mechanism, not non-determinism.
